name: Mashhad International Airport
before:
Iran's second busiest airport after Tehran Mehrabad, serving Mashhad in Razavi Khorasan province. It handled more than 10 million passengers in 2016, a record at the time, along with 86,681 tonnes of cargo.

There are three terminals and the split is unusual. Terminal 1 is domestic, Terminal 2 international and Terminal 3 is dedicated to Hajj flights, so check which building a client needs.

The route map reaches 57 destinations: 30 Iranian cities plus 27 across Central Asia, the Middle East, East Asia and Europe.

It is a joint civilian airport and military airbase, so parts of the site are not public.
after:
Mashhad's international airport.

Iran closed its airspace after the United States and Israel struck the country on 28 February 2026. Mashhad reopened in mid-April, but Iranian airspace can still close at short notice, and European regulators tell their airlines not to fly in it at any altitude.

New US sanctions from 23 September 2026 are aimed at shutting Iranian airlines out of international flying, and Turkish Airlines has suspended its Iran flights until at least March 2027.

The FCDO advises against all travel to Iran, and the US government tells its citizens not to travel there for any reason.

claims.note: Coordinates put it 7.8 km south east of the GeoNames centre of Mashhad.

claims.claim: second busiest after Mehrabad, Razavi Khorasan
claims.wasBefore: Iran's second busiest airport after Tehran Mehrabad, serving Mashhad in Razavi Khorasan province.
claims.why: The ranking and the province rest on Wikipedia alone; the Iranian airports company's statistics site and the airport's own site time out. Kept as Mashhad's international airport.

claims.claim: over 10 million passengers in 2016, record, 86,681 tonnes cargo
claims.wasBefore: It handled more than 10 million passengers in 2016, a record at the time, along with 86,681 tonnes of cargo.

claims.claim: three terminals: T1 domestic, T2 international, T3 Hajj
claims.wasBefore: There are three terminals and the split is unusual. Terminal 1 is domestic, Terminal 2 international and Terminal 3 is dedicated to Hajj flights, so check which building a client needs.
claims.why: Only Wikipedia; the operator's site (mashhad.airport.ir) times out and the web archive is blocked by the proxy.

claims.wasBefore: The route map reaches 57 destinations: 30 Iranian cities plus 27 across Central Asia, the Middle East, East Asia and Europe.
claims.why: Undated in the source and overtaken by the 2026 war and sanctions.

claims.claim: joint civilian airport and military airbase
claims.wasBefore: It is a joint civilian airport and military airbase, so parts of the site are not public.
claims.why: Wikipedia's sentence is taken almost word for word from GlobalSecurity, which it cites, so the two are one source, and GlobalSecurity's account runs only to 2008. 'Parts of the site are not public' had no source at all.
